title: The Mali Empire and Great Zimbabwe
examples: What were the main sources of wealth for the Mali Empire?
How did the trade routes connect Timbuktu and Great Zimbabwe?
What makes the architecture of Great Zimbabwe so unique?

explain.say: Today we are learning about two great West African civilizations. We will explore the Mali Empire and Great Zimbabwe. These powerful societies flourished long ago.

draw.text: The Mali Empire and Great Zimbabwe

explain.say: First we learn about Mansa Musa, a very wealthy ruler. He was the emperor of the Mali Empire. His wealth was famous across the world.
Next we look at Timbuktu, which was a major center for learning. It became famous for its libraries and scholars. Many important books were kept there.
Our third point is the stone city of Great Zimbabwe. This impressive structure was built without mortar. It shows advanced engineering skills.
In everyday life, the importance of trade is clear to see. Goods moved along established routes. These routes connected different cultures and economies.
A common mistake is thinking all great African civilizations were similar. They developed unique cultures and economies. Each had its own distinct achievements.

faq.q: What was the primary source of wealth for the Mali Empire?
faq.a: The Mali Empire was extremely wealthy mainly because of its control over the gold trade. Gold was a highly valued commodity across many regions.
asks: Where did the Mali get its money?

faq.q: Why was Timbuktu such an important place?
faq.a: Timbuktu was important because it was a major center for Islamic scholarship and learning. It housed many important manuscripts and scholars.
asks: Was Timbuktu just a trading post?

faq.a: Great Zimbabwe was constructed using massive dry-stone walls. These walls were built without the use of any mortar or cement.
asks: Did they use cement for the walls?
What material was used for the buildings?

faq.q: Did these empires trade with each other?
faq.a: While they were both powerful, the primary trade links connected these areas to the wider Mediterranean and North African worlds. The goods moved along established routes.
Mansa Musa was a powerful and famous emperor who ruled the Mali Empire. His pilgrimage to Mecca showed the world his immense riches.

facts: The Mali Empire controlled vital gold and salt trade routes.
Timbuktu was renowned as a center for Islamic learning and trade.
Great Zimbabwe is famous for its impressive dry-stone architecture.
Mansa Musa's wealth was legendary, especially during his Hajj journey.

quiz.say: The primary wealth source for the Mali Empire was:
quiz.why: The trade of gold was the main reason for the empire's great power and wealth.

wrong.1: While slaves were part of the trade, gold was the primary source of imperial wealth.
wrong.2: Salt was a vital trade good, but gold was the commodity that brought the most fame and wealth.
wrong.3: Books were important in Timbuktu, but they did not power the entire empire.

quiz.say: The stone structures at Great Zimbabwe show skill in:
quiz.why: The characteristic feature of Great Zimbabwe is its massive walls built using only stacked stone.

wrong.0: While metalworking occurred, the defining architectural feature is the stone work itself.
wrong.2: The construction method is known for avoiding any binding material like mortar.
wrong.3: The primary visible construction material and technique involve stone masonry.

quiz.say: If you were tracing the intellectual history of West Africa, which location would you focus on?
quiz.why: Timbuktu is specifically noted for its vast libraries and scholarly traditions.

wrong.0: The desert was the barrier, but Timbuktu was the destination of the learning.
wrong.2: The Mali Empire was a political and economic power, not primarily known for its libraries.
wrong.3: Great Zimbabwe is famous for its physical stone structures, not its scholarly collections.
